newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan constructions, financials fall on rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan constructions, financials fall on rate hike.

text.p: Taiwan's construction and financial shares fell at mid-session on Friday, reflecting jitters over slightly higher capital requirements for investments after the central bank's modest rate hikes, brokers said.
* At 0250 GMT, financial index down 1.02 percent.

* The central bank on Thursday announced a modest tightening of monetary policy by raising rediscount rate to 5.25 percent from 5.00 and accommodations against secured loans to 5.625 percent from 5.375, effective from Friday.

* Oliver Fang, senior analyst of National Securities: "The interest rate hikes, although only symbolic, create a reflex reaction that investment capital for investment could be tightened in constructions and financials -- sectors which typically rely on loans."
* Fang: "But the jitters are not likely to last, unless of course the central bank launches more substantial actions."
* "Big Three" state-run banks -- Chang Hwa, First Commercial and Hua Nan -- fell T$2, T$2 and T$1.50 respectively to T$121, T$121 and T$131.50.
